_note:
A GEARED CONTAINER FEEDER ON hull_150x32 — 150 x 32 m, the largest hull in the
catalog and the first thing built at this size. Built from the trawler's kit and nothing else:
one `from_hull` sheer band, seven authored `edges[]` runs, raked plates for every piece of
superstructure, spars and wires for the gear.

1. THE BULWARK IS `from_hull`, AND ON THIS HULL THAT IS THE RIGHT CALL. The trawler had to
   author its sheer because `sheer_bulwark_spec`'s derived curve was too polite for a working
   boat. full_bodied is the form that derivation was written for: bow_keel_rise 0.18 over 7.0 m
   of freeboard puts the cap 2.44 m above the build plane at the stem, 1.18 amidships and 1.53
   at the transom — a shallow, bow-dominant sheer, which is what a box freighter has. Nothing
   here restates a curve the hull already owns.

2. SCALE IS THE WHOLE EXERCISE, AND IT IS NOT THE TRAWLER SCALED UP. The trawler's deckhouse is
   2.74 m to the boat deck; this house is 21.4 m to the monkey island and 32.6 m to the funnel
   cap. The bulwark is the SAME 1.30 m on both, because it is a fall barrier set by the 1.8 m
   figure and not by the ship. That contrast is the reason the figure stands on the forecastle
   here: at 150 m a figure on the aft deck is four pixels.

3. THE LONG CONTAINER. The owner: "4x1 containers for larger ships". ContainerUnit's cubed unit
   is 4 m on a side, so four cells by one is 16.0 x 4.0 x 4.0 m. Drawn 15.80 x 3.94 x 3.80 with
   a 0.20 top rail in a darker tone: a stack of same-height slabs with no seam reads as ONE
   block, and the rail is what draws the tier line. Six rows at 4.16 m pitch leaves a 3.2 m
   walkway outboard of the coaming on both sides — seven rows fits the boxes and leaves 1.1 m,
   which is not a walkway.

   Each container is ONE plate: the quad is the horizontal mid-plane and the thickness is the
   height, so a box costs 12 triangles and one collider box. That is why the ship can be FULL.

4. THE RACK IS AN OPEN-TOP BAY. Cell guides are what "racks" means on a container ship — paired
   vertical angles at every cell corner that a box is lowered into, so it needs no lashing. On a
   normal bay they are under the hatch cover and invisible, so bay 3 is open-topped: the guides
   run from 9.4 m below the build plane to 14.6 m above it, tied athwartships and fore-and-aft
   at three levels and braced diagonally on both outboard faces, with boxes standing in them
   three tiers below deck and three above. Two of the six cells are deliberately short so the
   guides show bare — a rack you cannot see is not evidence of a rack.

5. THE STOW IS NOT UNIFORM. Tier counts run 2 to 4 by row and by bay and one row is empty. A
   stow at a constant height is a brick, and the silhouette of a container ship is made almost
   entirely of the top line of its stacks.

6. TWO CRANES, ONE OF THEM WORKING. Pedestal, slewing house, A-frame, a jib with two chords
   either side of it so it reads as a lattice rather than a pipe, luffing pendants and — on the
   after crane — hoist falls down to a spreader with an orange box in it, hanging over the open
   bay. The forward crane is luffed up and parked. A crane with nothing hanging off it is a mast.

7. SIX TIERS, EVERY ONE WITH A WINDOW BAND. Tiers 2 to 5 set back 0.55 m on each side and 0.9 m
   forward of the one below, and each set-back leaves a walkway that carries a railing run. The
   bridge deck is WIDER than the block under it — the wings hang out over the ship's side — and
   its windscreen rakes 1.15 m forward over 4.0 m. Bands, not punched holes: at this framing a
   dark value reads as glass and a punched hole reads as damage.

8. THE FORECASTLE IS SEPARATE AND RAISED, with its own sheer on top of the hull's: 3.20 m above
   the build plane at the break, 3.92 at the stem. Its side plating and its bulwark are ONE
   sheet of steel, which is what they are on a ship, and the `from_hull` bulwark passes behind
   them. A breakwater rakes 25 degrees aft across the deck between the break and bay 1.

COLOUR DOES VALUE WORK, FOR FREE. Dark topsides that the bulwark plating merges into, a bone cap
so the sheer is the lightest line on the hull, a cream house against a dark grey deck, near-black
glass, an oxide-red funnel with a black top, orange cranes and lifeboat, and ten container
liveries. Squinted, that is six values and the stacks are where the hue lives.

GENERATED. The numbers, the stow pattern and the crane geometry live in the generator; the JSON
is the interface.
